subsystems.name: OPM sensor
subsystems.role: converts femtotesla-scale magnetic fields from neuronal currents into an optical signal.

subsystems.name: Magnetic shielding and field control
subsystems.role: suppresses Earth's field and environmental noise so the sensors can work in the spin-exchange relaxation-free (SERF) regime.

subsystems.name: Sensor helmet and cabling
subsystems.role: holds dozens to hundreds of sensors close to the scalp in a wearable arrangement.

subsystems.name: Laser distribution
subsystems.role: delivers stabilised pump and probe light to every sensor.

subsystems.name: Data acquisition and real-time control
subsystems.role: digitises sensor outputs, keeps fields stable, and reconstructs brain sources.

subsystems.name: Subject interface and motion tracking
subsystems.role: presents stimuli, records responses, and tracks head position for movement-tolerant recordings.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the vapour cells
buildSteps.detail: Glass cells a few millimetres across are filled with a droplet of rubidium and a buffer gas, then sealed. They must hold a controlled alkali-metal vapour for years.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the sensors
buildSteps.detail: Each sensor packs a small laser, optics, a vapour cell, heaters and a photodetector into a housing roughly the size of a matchbox, with internal shields to reject stray fields.

buildSteps.title: Build the shielded room
buildSteps.detail: Several layers of mu-metal and aluminium enclose the recording space. Active coils cancel the remaining static field down to a few nanotesla or less, and degaussing coils remove trapped magnetism.

buildSteps.title: Make the helmet
buildSteps.detail: A participant's head is scanned to design a helmet that places each sensor within a few millimetres of the scalp. The helmet is 3D-printed in lightweight material with pockets for the sensors.

buildSteps.title: Install and cable the array
buildSteps.detail: Sensors are fitted into the helmet and their optical fibres and electrical cables are routed so they do not tug on the head or add magnetic noise.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate the system
buildSteps.detail: The room is degaussed, residual fields are nulled, and each sensor's noise floor (often around 5–15 fT/√Hz) and cross-talk are measured before use.

buildSteps.title: Commission acquisition and software
buildSteps.detail: Real-time field control, head-motion tracking and source-reconstruction pipelines are set up and tested with a phantom — a known magnetic source placed at known positions.

buildSteps.title: Validate with human subjects
buildSteps.detail: Recordings of evoked responses and spontaneous brain rhythms are compared against cryogenic SQUID MEG and EEG, followed by clinical validation for conditions such as epilepsy.

prerequisites.why: the sensors only reach femtotesla sensitivity when operated near zero field and at high spin-exchange relaxation-free temperature.
rubidium must be pumped and probed with light of a precise wavelength and very stable frequency.

prerequisites.tech: Magnetic shielding and active field cancellation
prerequisites.why: Earth's field is about 50 µT, roughly a billion times stronger than the brain signals being measured.
signals at the femtotesla level must be digitised without adding noise and with active field stabilisation.
wearable sensors allow movement, but software must track and correct for it so images stay sharp.
systems are sold for research and used in pilot clinical studies, but widespread clinical adoption awaits formal approvals.

pathway.milestone: commercial OPM-MEG systems used in research and pilot clinical studies, including epilepsy mapping
pathway.unlocks: wearable, cryogen-free brain imaging that can record subjects while they move.

pathway.milestone: regulatory clearance for clinical use, especially pre-surgical epilepsy evaluation and paediatric imaging
pathway.unlocks: routine hospital deployment where SQUID MEG is too costly or impractical.

pathway.milestone: integration with EEG and fMRI, plus real-time neurofeedback and natural-movement paradigms
pathway.unlocks: richer multimodal brain mapping and new neuroscience experiments.

pathway.milestone: portable, lower-cost MEG helmets and long-duration monitoring
pathway.unlocks: wider access to functional brain imaging in clinics and research settings.
